answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity in locked stake that unlocks only after a random draw, so an attacker cannot predict which epoch their bond clears. A farmer who plants one orchard keeps it through every tide because leaving early forfeits the harvest; likewise, one real operator holds one bond while a sybil farming a thousand identities must lock capital a thousand times, and the reef of locked deposits makes each fake identity a visible, costly commitment rather than a free alias.
